A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LangDriveCTRL with the same authors, core pipeline, and retained experiments. Their main text, supplementary sections, equations, tables, figures, and agent prompts are readable and can be matched despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original Waymo editing experiments, a 26-participant user study, object-grounding comparisons, and behavior and video refinement ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds video-reviewer experiments, hallucination measurements, another editing baseline, and downstream object-detection results.

M1.justification: v2 adds a Video Reviewer Agent to the existing rendering and diffusion pipeline. It evaluates realism and appearance preservation, then iteratively adjusts denoising strength and masked latent-space L2 guidance (Sections 3.7 and 8.3). This changes inference substantially; the existing grounding, counterfactual behavior generation, and trajectory-review procedures remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds downstream 3D object detection with BEVFormer trained using real and edited Waymo images (Section 6.5), extending evaluation from editing quality to the utility of generated training data. The original 30 editing scenes, object-grounding coverage, and editing operations are retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds ChronoEdit followed by Wan 2.2 as an evaluated composite baseline (Section 6.4, Table 10) and explicitly compares coarse outputs against ChatSim (Table 9). The original Cosmos/ChatSim editing comparisons and Grounding SAM/4DLangSplat grounding comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The new video ablation uses insertion/replacement instructions, three configurations, and appearance alignment alongside FID/FVD. New protocols introduce 3D Consistency, NTL-IoU, and detection AP at three IoU thresholds using 8,000 real frames with or without 8,000 edited frames. The counterfactual ablation also changes its stated instruction source from v1 Table 2 to v2 Table 1; identical results leave a rerun versus a cross-reference error unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 adds a controlled comparison separating coarse rendering, diffusion alone, and diffusion with video review; an explicit coarse-output comparison against ChatSim; and geometric/lane hallucination analysis with qualitative lane visualizations. Existing behavior and grounding analyses remain. The specific green-convertible appearance-failure case in v1 Figure 11 is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Random image selection for the grounding experiment remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Retained Table 1 quality/user-study scores and grounding/behavior results are unchanged. New results include video-reviewer appearance alignment of 85.28% versus 65.47% without review, coarse-to-refined 3D Consistency of 74.07 to 72.64 and NTL-IoU of 52.11 to 50.96, additional comparator scores, and detection AP@0.5 of 0.0533 versus 0.0635 with edited training data. Runtime values and accounting also change. The new video-ablation results do not establish a same-setting performance change from v1.

T1.justification: v2 Section 8.3 adds mathematical definitions for video refinement, particularly the masked residual, L2 loss, and scaled noise-prediction update in Equations 7–9. This is a localized extension of the formulation. The scene-graph definition, counterfactual Cartesian product, and compatibility constraints are retained; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list expand the central contribution to feedback-driven refinement of both behavior and video, including appearance preservation through the new Video Reviewer Agent. The introduction also adds comparable latency as a contribution. The supported editing operations and nearly twofold instruction-alignment claim remain.

C2.justification: v2 develops the realism-versus-appearance tradeoff and explains how video review addresses it, interprets the coarse comparison as evidence for the agentic architecture, and acknowledges mild geometric/lane degradation from diffusion. Runtime interpretation changes from fastest to comparable. Conversely, the explicit pedestrian-editing limitation and the rare-vehicle training-bias explanation are removed; the median-barrier failure remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds the Video Reviewer prompt, masked-frame inputs, bounded averaging rules for parameter updates, a five-iteration cap, and detailed latent-guidance equations. It also identifies TwinLiteNet for lane evaluation and expands runtime accounting. Existing agent prompts and training settings are largely retained, but v1's specification of Cosmos-Predict2.5 Base rather than Auto is omitted.

R1.justification: The related-work families and capability comparison remain, with stronger emphasis on multimodal reasoning and feedback, including an updated contrast with SimSplat. New citations support the added components and evaluations, including SDEdit, ChronoEdit, Wan, WorldScore, DriveDreamer4D, and BEVFormer. Citations to earlier collaborative-agent inspirations and pedestrian-animation work are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten around three shortcomings of prior methods and two motivating insights. Runtime discussion moves into the main experiments, and supplementary experiments are reorganized into numbered subsections. Much of the existing method exposition and original agent prompts remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column to a single-column format with extensive resizing and rearrangement. Figure 2 gains a video-review feedback loop; new reviewer, comparator, and lane-preservation figures and experimental tables are added. Runtime tables are restructured, the editing-capabilities figure is rearranged and loses its removal panel, and the convertible-failure figure is removed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens its treatment of v1's documented appearance-drift problem. The new controlled ablation raises appearance alignment from 65.47% to 85.28% with review while retaining similar FID, and the added coarse comparison and hallucination measurements clarify both contributions and tradeoffs. Detailed reviewer documentation further supports reproducibility. Removing the explicit pedestrian limitation, rare-vehicle failure discussion, and Cosmos variant disclosure weakens transparency, but the methodological and evidential gains outweigh these losses. The original headline benchmark scores remain unchanged.
